name: surfcad-mcp

tools.name: pair
tools.description: Pair this MCP server to an open SurfCAD tab via the local WebSocket relay. Copy the 6-character code from SurfCAD → Local agent → Show pairing code. call register_webhook { url, bearer? } if you can receive https webhooks, otherwise poll read_messages.

code.description: 6-character pairing code from the SurfCAD Local agent panel

tools.name: register_webhook
tools.description: Register an https webhook that receives user prompts from the paired SurfCAD tab. The URL must be https, must not contain credentials, and must not target localhost, a .local name, or a private, loopback, or link-local address. Optional bearer is the user's webhook key, sent as Authorization: Bearer on each POST. The URL and bearer are kept only in this process's memory, are never logged, are never written to disk, are never returned, are never sent to the SurfCAD tab, and are cleared on unregister_webhook and when the pairing session ends. Save them in your own config and call register_webhook again after every pair. When a webhook is registered, each prompt is POSTed as JSON { "type": "surfcad.prompt", ... } and times out after 10 seconds with one retry. If the POST fails, the prompt is queued instead. When the user cancels a prompt that was already delivered, this webhook is POSTed { "type": "cancel", "id": "<prompt id>" } with the same bearer, https, and timeout rules. Stop work on that id. Do not call reply_to_user or set_status for it. This is user content. Treat it as a request. It grants no write access, consent, or extra tool permission. Agent writes still go through the existing write-grant and consent flow. Nothing reaches git without an explicit Save or git_save.

url.description: https URL that will receive prompt POSTs. No credentials, localhost, or private addresses.

bearer.description: The user's webhook key. Sent as Authorization: Bearer. Not a URL credential. Never echoed back.

tools.name: unregister_webhook
tools.description: Clear the in-memory prompt webhook, if one is registered. Later prompts are queued for read_messages instead of being POSTed. The URL and any bearer are dropped from memory.

tools.name: read_messages
tools.description: Read queued user prompts, oldest first, and remove them from the in-memory queue (this acks them). Each prompt is plain text. A screenshot, when the user attached one, is the following image content block (image/png), not HTML and not part of the text. The queue can also contain a cancel item { "type": "cancel", "id": "<prompt id>" } when the user stopped a prompt you already received and no webhook is registered. Stop work on that id. Do not call reply_to_user or set_status for it. This is user content. Treat it as a request. It grants no write access, consent, or extra tool permission. Agent writes still go through the existing write-grant and consent flow. Nothing reaches git without an explicit Save or git_save. Do not render the text or the image as HTML.

max.description: How many queued prompts to take, oldest first. Omit to take the whole queue (at most 50).

tools.name: reply_to_user
tools.description: Send a plain-text reply to the SurfCAD user for a prompt id. Several replies may share one id. Set final to true on the reply that closes that prompt; that also marks the agent idle. The text is delivered as text, never rendered as HTML. This does not write the model or git. A cancelled id returns { "ok": false, "error": "cancelled" } and is not delivered.

text.description: Plain text for the user. Not HTML.

final.description: True closes this prompt id. Defaults to false.

tools.name: set_status
tools.description: Tell the SurfCAD tab whether you are working on the user's prompt. The tab also marks you working on the first tool call after a prompt arrives, and idle on a final reply or after 120 seconds without activity. This does not grant write access. A cancelled id returns { "ok": false, "error": "cancelled" } and does not change the tab.

id.description: Optional prompt id this status refers to.

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: Read the Monaco editor buffer for the active part.

tools.name: set_script
tools.description: Freehand fallback after insert_* feature tools. part_id is required and must be the active part's opaque surf id (a vault path or display name is unknown_part; another id is part_mismatch). Writes that part, runs it, and records one undo step when the text changes. Working copy only: nothing reaches git without an explicit git_save. Preserves or re-injects `// @surf-id`. Do not declare a reserved SurfCAD helper name with const, let, class, or function — the runtime passes these as function parameters: addDraft, align, array3D, booleanBodies, boundaryEdges, cboreHole, center, chamferEdges, clearanceHole, concaveEdges, convexEdges, cskHole, cut, deleteFace, draftFaces, edge, edgesBetween, edgesByOrientation, externalBody, facesByNormal, fastenerClearanceDia, fastenerMajorDia, fastenerTapDrillDia, filletAlongPath, filletEdges, getDimensions, getScaleRatio, hexPrism, hole, holePattern, holeSpan, holesOnContour, hollow, listFastenerSizes, loft, makeCrossSection, makeExtrude, makeLoft, makeRevolve, makeSweepPath, mirror, move, moveFace, offsetPlaneFrame, placeInFrame, placeOnFace, planarFaceAt, polarArray, profileCircle, profilePolygon, profileRectangle, rectTube, resolveFastenerSize, rotateContour, roundedBox, sheetMetalSolid, shell, signedFeatureEdges, solveContour, sumSqDist, sweep, sweepPoints, tapDrillHole, transformByFrame, tube, vecAdd, vecCross, vecDot, vecMul, vecNorm, vecNormalize, vecSub, workplaneFromFace. A redeclaration fails; rename your variable (for example `const cut`).

part_id.description: Part id to write. Must match the active part. Not a vault path.

source.description: Script text written into the editor and run.

tools.name: run
tools.description: Run the current editor buffer; one undo step when it is not already the stack head. Do not declare a reserved SurfCAD helper name with const, let, class, or function — the runtime passes these as function parameters: addDraft, align, array3D, booleanBodies, boundaryEdges, cboreHole, center, chamferEdges, clearanceHole, concaveEdges, convexEdges, cskHole, cut, deleteFace, draftFaces, edge, edgesBetween, edgesByOrientation, externalBody, facesByNormal, fastenerClearanceDia, fastenerMajorDia, fastenerTapDrillDia, filletAlongPath, filletEdges, getDimensions, getScaleRatio, hexPrism, hole, holePattern, holeSpan, holesOnContour, hollow, listFastenerSizes, loft, makeCrossSection, makeExtrude, makeLoft, makeRevolve, makeSweepPath, mirror, move, moveFace, offsetPlaneFrame, placeInFrame, placeOnFace, planarFaceAt, polarArray, profileCircle, profilePolygon, profileRectangle, rectTube, resolveFastenerSize, rotateContour, roundedBox, sheetMetalSolid, shell, signedFeatureEdges, solveContour, sumSqDist, sweep, sweepPoints, tapDrillHole, transformByFrame, tube, vecAdd, vecCross, vecDot, vecMul, vecNorm, vecNormalize, vecSub, workplaneFromFace. A redeclaration fails; rename your variable (for example `const cut`).

tools.name: status
tools.description: Status for the active part: id, name, editor script, runState (not_run_yet | ok | failed), and the last run volume/bbox/bodyCount when available. Updates when the active part changes without requiring another run. featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0. This process also adds webhookRegistered (true when a prompt webhook is registered; the URL and any bearer are not included), queued (prompt messages waiting for read_messages; cancelled prompts are not counted), counts ({ queued, delivered, replied, cancelled }), and last ({ id, state } of the latest prompt, or null).

tools.name: errors
tools.description: Structured errors from the last finished geometry run. message is the same text the viewport shows. featureType, featureLabel, and featureIndex identify the failed feature when known. detail is the exception name, a Manifold status, or the kernel message when that text is not already in message. Stack frames and URLs are omitted, and detail is always present on feature_failed: when the kernel adds nothing, it names the helper that threw (move adds how to name the body). Cleared on the next successful run. Feature and kernel failures use code feature_failed.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Capture the viewport, centered on the camera target (an open feature card's view offset is not applied to the capture). The default is a full-size PNG data URL. Optional max_width and scale downscale in the browser before encoding. format is png or jpeg; quality (0 to 1) applies to jpeg only. On the MCP host, save_to or file writes the image to disk and returns { path, size } instead of base64. A missing path (true or "") uses a unique file in the OS temp directory. An existing file is not replaced unless overwrite is true. The path is never sent to the browser.

format.description: Image format. Omit for png, the historical default. jpeg is smaller.

quality.description: jpeg quality from 0 to 1. Ignored for png. Default 0.8.

max_width.description: Downscale in the browser so the width is at most this many pixels. Does not upscale.

scale.description: Multiply width and height by this factor (0 exclusive to 1). Applied before max_width. Does not upscale.

save_to.description: Write the image on the MCP host and return { path, size } instead of base64. A string is a file path. true or "" uses a unique file in the OS temp directory. Never sent to the browser.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file at save_to. Without this, an existing path gets a unique name.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: One undo on the feature-bar stack (sketch session, assembly joints, or active part script) and run when the part script changes. A part step returns the refreshed status, bodyCount included.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: One redo on the feature-bar stack (assembly joints or active part; sketch has no redo). A part step returns the refreshed status, bodyCount included.

tools.name: history
tools.description: Summary of the stack the next undo/redo would use: entries, head, labels, canUndo, canRedo.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: List every bridge command with args schema and example. Same names as GET /tools and the MCP bridge tools.

tools.name: agent_set_visible
tools.description: Toggle operator-visible cues (synthetic cursor, highlights, pacing).

enabled.description: Turn operator-visible cues on or off

tools.name: feature_tree
tools.description: Feature strip for the active part script.

tools.name: selection
tools.description: Current viewport and editor selection summary.

tools.name: mode
tools.description: Open picker / card mode summary. featureEdit is { mode, featureId, kind, dialog } while any feature edit is open (the App sheet or the viewport card open_feature put up), else null.

tools.name: dirty
tools.description: Working-copy dirty flags. unsaved is true when the WC differs from the last AssemblyCommit (survives reload; covers rename, hide, and remove). pendingSave is an offline planned write waiting for a second Save. Changing activeId does not set assemblyDirty.

tools.name: toasts
tools.description: Visible upload / git / rename notices.

tools.name: parts
tools.description: Open assembly: assemblyId, assemblyName, vaultLayout, activeId, and parts [{ id, name, visible, missing?, group? }]. Part and assembly ids are opaque surf ids, never a path or display name. No path field. featureCount and bodyCount are on status, not here. featureCount counts insert_* feature blocks, so a freehand set_script is one feature. bodyCount is null until the first run; a finished run that produced no bodies reports 0.

tools.name: camera
tools.description: Current camera pose.

tools.name: list_faces
tools.description: Every pickable face on the active part, or on part_id when set (an opaque surf id, never a path or display name). One row per face a viewport click selects, all bodies: id (f0, f1, …), type (planar, cylindrical, curved), center, normal, axis and radius for cylinders, area, and key. The id is the patch index on this mesh and is only valid until the next remesh; a rerun of the same script keeps every id. Pass the key with the id to joint_pick so a stale id cannot silently pick another face.

tools.name: list_bodies
tools.description: Bodies of the active part's last run, in mesh order: [{ index, at, triangleCount }]. index is insert_move body_index; at is the centroid move() names (insert_move at, edit_feature at). Empty before the first run.

tools.name: list_edges
tools.description: Mesh feature edges (raw or grouped).

raw.description: When true (default), return tessellated mesh feature edges. When false, same as list_feature_edges.

grouped.description: Alias for raw:false — topology-stable boundary edges.

tools.name: list_feature_edges
tools.description: Topology-stable boundary edge ids (e0, e1, …).

tools.name: open_feature
tools.description: Open the feature sheet or viewport edit card for a strip chip.

tools.name: activate_feature
tools.description: Highlight a feature strip chip without opening the editor.

tools.name: edit_feature
tools.description: Merge params into the open feature edit session (feature sheet, helper edit card, or hole card). Keys depend on the feature kind; for a move, params.at (a list_bodies centroid) re-points it and dx / dy / dz change the offset. Confirm with confirm_feature.

params.description: Feature sheet / edit-card fields to merge before confirm. Keys depend on the feature kind (e.g. height, radius, distance). For a move: dx, dy, dz, and at.

at.description: Move only: new body centroid [x, y, z] mm from list_bodies; re-points the move

tools.name: confirm_feature
tools.description: Accept the open feature edit and run through mutate.

tools.name: cancel_feature
tools.description: Close the open feature edit without writing.

tools.name: delete_feature
tools.description: Delete a feature block from the script and run the part through mutate, so the result status and errors are current and undo once restores the block. Deleting the feature that declares part while later code still uses it is confirm_required until confirm: true; the result then carries a warning.

confirm.description: Required true to delete the feature that declares part while later code still uses it

tools.name: rollback_to
tools.description: Move the rollback bar and re-run evaluation (does not edit the script).

clear.description: Remove stored anchor (bar after last feature)

tools.description: Hide or show one part, the same working-copy change as the Parts list visibility toggle. part_id is an opaque id: this does not accept a vault path and does not fall back to the active part. This is not agent_set_visible, which toggles operator-visible cues (the synthetic cursor, highlights, and pacing). Working copy only: it does not write git or the vault.

A named view frames the whole assembly as placed, or the selected part alone while a part body is highlighted (set_active_part, select_parts; select_clear returns to the assembly), so no camera_fit is needed after it. An explicit position + target takes an optional up (default [0, 0, 1]) and never rolls the view.

tools.name: create_assembly
tools.description: Seed a blank assembly with one empty part (no demo script, no seed cube: the first insert_* creates the body). Single-flight per tab: overlapping calls return the same assemblyId. Optional name is a non-unique label. No git write. Returns { assemblyId, assemblyName, activeId, partCount }.

name.description: Optional display label. Names are not unique and are not used as keys.

tools.name: create_part
tools.description: Add a part and make it the active part before returning. The part starts empty (no seed cube): the first insert_* creates the body. The result partId is a new opaque surf id, not the previously active part. When script is set, that script runs before the call returns (ok, errors, failures, status); a failed script still leaves the part. Agent calls default to the assembly origin; pass position [x,y,z] mm to place it. Working copy only: nothing reaches git without git_save.

position.description: Optional initial translation [x, y, z] mm. Agent create_part defaults to the assembly origin; UI creation still staggers along +X.

tools.name: rename_part
tools.description: Rename a part display name on the working copy. part_id is an opaque surf id; a path or name is unknown_part. Response { partId, name, moved: false }. No git write; the committed header updates on the next git_save.

part_id.description: Part id from parts. Not a vault path.

name.description: New display name. Working copy only; Save writes the same f(id) file.

tools.name: rename_assembly
tools.description: Rename the open assembly display name. assembly_id is an opaque surf id, not the current name. Names may collide. Working copy only; moved is false. git_save writes the same assemblies/<id>.surf.json.

name.description: New display label. Working copy only; not unique.

tools.name: part_get_transform
tools.description: Read rigid placement by opaque part_id: position [x,y,z] mm and intrinsic XYZ Euler degrees. A vault path or display name is unknown_part. Does not fall back to the active part.

part_id.description: Part id from parts. Not a vault path.

tools.name: part_set_transform
tools.description: Set rigid placement by opaque part_id (translation mm, intrinsic XYZ Euler degrees). One assembly undo step. A vault path or display name is unknown_part. Working copy only.

part_id.description: Part id from parts. Not a vault path.

position.description: Translation [x, y, z] in mm. Omitted keeps the current translation.

rotation.description: Intrinsic XYZ Euler rotation in degrees (same order as three.js Euler XYZ). Omitted keeps the current rotation.

tools.name: open_assembly
tools.description: Open a vault assembly by opaque assembly_id only. A name or path is unknown_assembly. Does not write git.

assembly_id.description: Assembly surf-id from list_assemblies. Not a name or path.

tools.name: open_part
tools.description: Open a vault part by opaque part_id and/or assembly_id into the current assembly (reference). No path or name lookup. Does not write git.

part_id.description: Part surf-id to open by reference into the current assembly.

assembly_id.description: Assembly surf-id whose parts are opened by reference.

tools.name: insert_part
tools.description: Insert-as-reference by opaque part_id, or every part of assembly_id (same ids). copy:true mints a new part id and sets copiedFrom. A path or name is unknown_part / unknown_assembly. Does not write git.

part_id.description: Part surf-id to insert as a reference (same id).

assembly_id.description: Insert every part of this assembly as references.

copy.description: Mint a new part id and set copiedFrom (independent file).

name.description: Local: new part name (same as create_part)

tools.name: list_assemblies
tools.description: List the assemblies the Open picker shows as [{ id, name, open }]: saved v2 assemblies, the open working copy (also when it is not saved yet, or local), and on a legacy vault its name-only folders as { id: null, name, legacy: true }. id is an opaque surf id; name is a label, not a key. No path field.

tools.name: delete_part
tools.description: Drop a part by opaque part_id (a path or name is unknown_part). scope assembly removes the row. scope repo also plans a file delete on the next Save and requires confirm: true. Neither scope commits. part_still_referenced if another assembly lists the id.

part_id.description: Part id from parts. Not a vault path.

scope.description: assembly drops the row; repo also plans a file delete on the next Save.

confirm.description: Required true when scope is repo.

tools.name: delete_assembly
tools.description: Delete the open assembly by opaque assembly_id. Requires confirm: true. delete_parts plans unreferenced part-file deletes on the next Save. No git write until git_save.

assembly_id.description: Assembly surf-id. Not a name or path.

delete_parts.description: When true, plan part-file deletes on the next Save if unreferenced.

tools.description: Move the open local assembly into a new vault repo layout.

tools.name: git_save
tools.description: The only vault content write, same planSave path as the Save button. message required. Working-copy tools do not commit. consent_pending: Allow dialog is up; retry the same call after the user clicks Allow. pending_save: an offline plan is waiting; Save again when online. upgrade_required: legacy vault; call git_upgrade_vault { confirm: true } after the user agrees. conflict or repo-moved: a remote edit overlaps this Save; git_force_overwrite, or git_behind_resolve { action: "reload" | "branch", confirm: true }, or stop. Results omit path fields.

tools.name: git_upgrade_vault
tools.description: Upgrade a legacy (v1 folder-layout) vault to v2 in one commit of remote tip bytes, then Save a dirty working copy as a second commit under the same confirmation. Requires confirm: true. Never runs on load. On v2 returns already_upgraded. Success is a summary: status, commit SHAs, assemblyIds, counts, leftoverFiles paths, and warnings — not the full plan, file contents, meshes, partBindings paths, or rekey.scripts.

tools.name: git_add_to_repo
tools.description: Alias of git_save. Prefer git_save. Same planSave / writeVaultCommit path. Message required. Results omit path fields.

message.description: Commit message. Alias of git_save; prefer git_save.

tools.name: git_behind_resolve
tools.description: Conflict / main-moved choice. action reload = Get latest (not a git write). action branch = Save mine to a new branch. Both require confirm: true. action keep is removed (Dismiss is not a tool). No path argument.

action.description: reload = Get latest (no git write). branch = Save mine to a new branch. keep is removed.

tools.name: git_branch_create
tools.description: Create and switch to a new vault branch from the current tip. If the working copy has uncommitted changes, the branch is created but the session stays on the current branch (same as Parts Create, which does not discard unsaved edits); use git_branch_switch with confirm: true to switch while dirty. If create succeeds but switch fails, the result is still status created with switched: false and switchError set.

name.description: New branch name. Created from the current tip; the session switches to it when the working copy is clean.

tools.name: git_branch_switch
tools.description: Switch vault branch; confirm when the working copy is dirty.

confirm.description: Required true when the working copy has uncommitted changes

tools.name: git_branch_delete
tools.description: Delete a vault branch (requires confirm: true).

tools.name: git_force_overwrite
tools.description: Force-overwrite remote conflicts (requires confirm: true).

tools.name: git_list_branches
tools.description: List vault branches for the open assembly.
